test: AP Macroeconomics Unit 4: The Financial Sector - Bonds and Interest Rates

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements about bond prices and market interest rates are true?
choices: Bond prices and market interest rates are inversely related.
When market interest rates rise, the prices of existing bonds fall.
When market interest rates fall, the prices of existing bonds fall.
A bond's face value changes each time market interest rates change.

questions.prompt: A bond has a $1,000 face value and a 5% coupon rate ($50 per year). If the market interest rate rises to 6%, which of the following are true?
choices: The existing bond will sell at a discount from its face value.
The bond's coupon payment rises to $60 per year.
Investors prefer newly issued 6% bonds, so demand for the existing bond falls.
The existing bond will sell at a premium above its face value.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would shift the demand for loanable funds to the right?
choices: Firms expect higher profits from new investment projects.
The government increases its budget deficit and borrows to finance it.
Households increase their saving.
Foreign investors increase their purchases of domestic financial assets.
The government runs a larger budget surplus.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would shift the supply of loanable funds to the right?
choices: An increase in the private saving rate
An increase in capital inflows from foreign investors
A move from a budget deficit to a budget surplus
An increase in the expected profitability of investment

questions.prompt: The nominal interest rate on a loan is 7% and expected inflation is 3%. Which of the following are true?
choices: The expected real interest rate is approximately 4%.
The expected real interest rate is approximately 10%.
If expected inflation rises to 5% and the nominal rate stays at 7%, the expected real rate falls to approximately 2%.
The nominal interest rate equals the real interest rate plus expected inflation (approximately).
The real interest rate is unaffected by changes in expected inflation if the nominal rate is fixed.

questions.prompt: Suppose the Federal Reserve conducts an open market purchase of government bonds. Which of the following are likely results?
choices: Bank reserves increase.
The money supply increases.
The nominal interest rate falls in the short run.
The price of government bonds falls.
The money supply curve shifts left.

questions.prompt: Which of the following actions by the Federal Reserve would tend to lower the federal funds rate?
choices: Buying government securities on the open market
Lowering the discount rate
Lowering the interest rate paid on reserve balances
Selling government securities on the open market
Raising the reserve requirement

questions.prompt: Which of the following correctly describe the concept of present value?
choices: The present value of a future payment is less than its future value when the interest rate is positive.
A higher interest rate lowers the present value of a future payment.
The longer the wait until a payment is received, the lower its present value.
Present value is unaffected by the interest rate.
Present value is always greater than future value.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are consistent with the crowding-out effect?
choices: Government deficit spending increases the demand for loanable funds.
The real interest rate rises as a result of government borrowing.
Private investment spending decreases.
The real interest rate falls as a result of government borrowing.
The supply of loanable funds increases enough to fully offset the new government borrowing.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements about the risk, return, and liquidity of financial assets are correct?
choices: Assets with higher risk generally must offer higher expected returns to attract investors.
Longer-term bonds generally have greater interest-rate-related price risk than shorter-term bonds.
Cash is the most liquid financial asset.
Stocks are more liquid than cash.
